title: subuid/subgid check can be confused by wrong $USER environment
body:
### Issue Description

The problem showed up when trying to run podman commands within a container environment. It showed up the only issue was a wrong `USER=` environment variable.

In my scenario podman continuously reported
```plaintext
Error: invalid configuration: the specified mapping 1:65535 in "/etc/subuid" includes the user UID
```
on every podman command.

Finally I found out that `USER=root` was set in the environment but I was running as a user. So it looks like the logic in

https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/7ac4011b5e591355863cd738a6b9c4a2411a70ba/pkg/rootless/rootless_linux.go#L111

can be easily confused by a wrong `USER` environment variable.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
```
podman run -it --net=host --security-opt label=disable --privileged \
    --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --device /dev/fuse:rw \
    --user user --userns=keep-id:uid=1000,gid=1000 --env USER=root \
    quay.io/containers/aio:latest
```
taken from https://github.com/podman-container-tools/image_build/tree/main/aio - please note the `--env USER=root`


### Describe the results you received

```plaintext
Error: invalid configuration: the specified mapping 1:65535 in "/etc/subuid" includes the user UID
```
Thus podman evaluates the `root:` entry in `/etc/subuid` not the one for `user`.

### Describe the results you expected

As far as I can say the code at https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/7ac4011b5e591355863cd738a6b9c4a2411a70ba/pkg/rootless/rootless_linux.go#L111 is a convenience/sanity check. May be it can be made robust against a wrong `USER=`

### podman info output

```yaml
v2026.10.26
```

### Podman in a container

Yes

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

Additional environment details

### Additional information

Additional information like issue happens only occasionally or issue happens with a particular architecture or on a particular setting

comments.body:
> v2026.10.26

That provides zero information to us. I have no idea what this version is supposed to be btw not that it particular matters here though.

Looking at the code we check the USER env before doing the actual user lookup through libc. I am not sure if there is a practical standard that says USER should be valid or not. In any case it sounds like bound for trouble doing that so the simple answer is fix you env.
But for podman I suppose nothing would break if we stop reading `USER` env there.
cc @giuseppe

> os.Getenv is an optimization because user.LookupId can be slow, I personally prefer to keep the faster version than having to workaround a broken env

ack yes that makes sense to me, lets close this then as invalid environment

@Luap99 
v2026.10.26 is the version of the `quay.io/containers/aio:latest` tag
```bash
podman run -it --net=host --security-opt label=disable --privileged \
    --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --device /dev/fuse:rw \
    --user user --userns=keep-id:uid=1000,gid=1000 --env USER=root \
    quay.io/containers/aio:v2026.10.26 podman --version
# podman version 5.8.9
```

Of course I fixed the broken USER env in the meanwhile. But the way to isolate that the USER env is the rootcause was troublesome.
Thus I wanted to provide this as feedback.
